sections.heading: C2 — Laws restraints and related issues
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Laws restraints and related issues

FACT_ID: sec15-R01 | anchor: A04
Voice knowledge tests are available on request for applicants who have difficulty reading. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec15-R02 | anchor: A04
Disability parking requires an authorized disability or disabled-veteran plate or placard and use of the vehicle by or to transport the eligible beneficiary. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec15-R03 | anchor: A04
An unlawfully parked vehicle in a disability space may be towed, with towing costs required to reclaim it. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec15-R04 | anchor: A04
Do not discard waste from a vehicle onto a highway, unconsenting public or private property, or state waters. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec15-R05 | anchor: A04
A driver may be fined for vehicle-occupant littering as well as the driver's own conduct. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec15-R06 | anchor: A04
A vehicle needs an authorized safety inspection every twelve months, with the sticker showing the next due date. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec15-R07 | anchor: A04
Safety inspection may be completed up to ninety days before expiration. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec15-R08 | anchor: A04
An officer noticing faulty equipment may require repair within five days to avoid a citation. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec15-R09 | anchor: A04
Before passing a bicycle, check for oncoming traffic and maintain at least four feet of clearance. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec15-R10 | anchor: A04
If necessary and safe to preserve four feet of bicycle clearance, a driver may cross a double yellow centerline. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec15-R11 | anchor: A04
A slower cyclist normally keeps right unless turning left, but this keep-right rule is waived where each direction has only one lane. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec15-R12 | anchor: A04
With one travel lane, a cyclist may use any portion to avoid hazards and stay clear of parked cars. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec15-R13 | anchor: A04
Do not turn across the path of a cyclist continuing straight on the road or shoulder. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec15-R14 | anchor: A04
Forcing a cyclist off the road can lead to criminal charges. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec15-R15 | anchor: A04
Cyclists must follow traffic laws but may travel below a posted minimum without an impeding-traffic citation. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec15-R16 | anchor: A04
Cyclists may ride on a shoulder or berm but are not required to use it. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec15-R17 | anchor: A05
Do not drive through or around a hazardous-road closure sign or traffic-control device. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec15-R18 | anchor: A05
A hazardous-road-closure conviction adds two points and can bring a fine up to 250 dollars. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec15-R19 | anchor: A05
If bypassing a closure brings an emergency response, the fine can reach 500 dollars and the driver is liable for response costs. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec15-R20 | anchor: A05
Before opening a door, check the rearview and side mirrors, then use the hand farther from the door. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec15-R21 | anchor: A05
The Dutch Reach turns the body toward approaching cyclists and helps prevent the door opening too fast. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec15-R22 | anchor: A05
Cyclists should stay at least three feet from parked cars, with or without bike lanes, to avoid opening doors. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]
